question.problem: In what direction does the function $g(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xyz$ increase most rapidly at the point $(1,0,-2)?$
question.worked_solution:
At a given point, a function $g(x,y,z)$ increases most rapidly in the direction of its gradient at that point.

So, we compute $∇g(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,0,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xyz),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xyz),\,\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-xyz)⟩ \\  & =⟨2x-yz,\,2y-xz,\,2z-xy⟩ \\ ∇g(1,0,-2) & =⟨2(1)-0(-2),2(0)-1(-2),2(-2)-1(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,2,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the function increases most rapidly in the direction of $⟨2,2,-4⟩.$
